connectors.name: Salesforce
connectors.keyActions: 25 active actions (6 deprecated): Get Account/Contact/Case/Opportunity/Product/User records (typed, OData params), Get records (generic, any object), Get record (by ID), Get record by External ID, Execute SOQL query (parameterized @params), Execute SOSL search, Create/Update(V3)/Delete/Upsert record, Send HTTP request, Bulk job ops (Create/Upload/Close/Get/Delete), Get object types, MCP server action (`mcp_SalesforceManagement`). OData filter: `eq`,`ne`,`gt`,`ge`,`lt`,`le`,`and`,`or`,`not` -- no `contains`/`startswith`. `$select`/`$top`/`$skip`/`$orderby` supported. Custom fields (`__c`) work in all params. Row limit: 2000 (Salesforce API) but 500KB response limit is usually binding. SOQL supports JOINs, aggregates, GROUP BY, date literals, relationship queries. Full deep-dive: `Build-Guides/CDW/agents/account-prospecting/research/salesforce-connector-deep-dive.md`

patterns.name: Web Content Extraction
patterns.naive: HTTP Request connector to fetch URL, pass raw HTML to AI prompt.
patterns.proven: Dedicated content extraction service that returns clean structured article data. Multiple implementation tiers available.
matchKeywords: Capability mentions extract from web, summarize website, read URL content, or web scraping
Integration lists HTTP connector with a URL-fetching purpose
Data flow includes: URL input → content extraction → AI processing
Customer is replacing a per-site scraping script (BeautifulSoup, Scrapy, Cheerio, etc.)

patterns.name: Document Generation
patterns.naive: Generate document content inline in the agent response (markdown or plain text), tell user to copy-paste.
patterns.proven: Power Automate flow with Word Online "Populate a Microsoft Word template" action. Agent collects data → triggers flow → flow fills template → returns SharePoint URL.
matchKeywords: Capability mentions generate report, create document, produce PDF, fill template
Output is a formatted document (not just a text response)
Document has a consistent structure (template-able)

patterns.name: Iterating Over N Items
patterns.naive: Topic YAML with a loop construct or repeated question nodes to process each item.
patterns.proven: Power Automate flow with "Apply to each" action. Agent collects the list → sends to flow → flow iterates and processes → returns aggregated result.
matchKeywords: Capability involves processing a list of items (approvals, tickets, records)
Data flow includes: for each X, do Y
Topic design would require repeating the same logic N times
User says batch, bulk, multiple, all items

patterns.name: File Upload in Teams Channel
patterns.naive: Accept file via topic variable, process directly in the agent.
patterns.proven: Stage files to SharePoint first, pass the SharePoint URL to the agent. Or use Power Automate flow triggered by file upload to a specific Teams channel/SharePoint folder.
matchKeywords: Capability mentions upload file, attach document, send PDF to agent
Channel is Teams (web chat file upload works differently)
Data flow includes: user provides file → agent processes file content

patterns.name: Complex Data Transformation
patterns.naive: AI prompt action to transform data (parse CSV, reformat JSON, calculate totals).
patterns.proven: Code interpreter action (if available) or Azure Function / Power Automate expression for deterministic transformations. Use AI only for unstructured-to-structured (e.g., extract fields from free text).
matchKeywords: Capability requires precise calculations (totals, averages, date math)
Data flow includes structured format conversion (CSV → JSON, XML → table)
Output must be deterministic (same input = same output every time)
Data volume exceeds ~50 rows or ~2000 tokens

patterns.name: Scheduled Batch Processing
patterns.naive: MCS scheduled trigger (Recurrence) to process batches of records at intervals.
patterns.proven: Power Automate scheduled flow handles the batch. Agent is invoked only for human-in-the-loop decisions or to report results.
matchKeywords: Capability mentions daily report, weekly sync, scheduled cleanup, batch update
Processing is headless (no user interaction during processing)
Data flow: timer → query records → process each → report/store results

patterns.name: Multi-System Orchestration
patterns.naive: Sequential MCP server or connector calls within a single topic, relying on generative orchestration to chain them.
patterns.proven: Power Automate flow with explicit action ordering, error handling per step, and transaction compensation. Agent sends the request → flow orchestrates → returns result.
matchKeywords: Capability requires data from 2+ different systems in a specific order
Data from system A is needed as input to system B
Any step failure should prevent subsequent steps (transactional)
Cross-system field mapping is needed

patterns.name: API with Complex Auth
patterns.naive: HTTP Request action with auth headers (API key, OAuth token) configured in topic YAML or connector.
patterns.proven: Custom connector with proper auth configuration, or Azure Function as auth proxy. Auth complexity lives outside the agent.
matchKeywords: Integration requires OAuth2 (authorization code, client credentials, or PKCE)
API uses certificate-based authentication
API requires multi-step token exchange
Integration mentions SSO, delegated permissions, or service account

patterns.name: Large Dataset Processing
patterns.naive: Connector query action that returns all records, process in topic.
patterns.proven: Power Automate flow with pagination enabled, server-side filtering, and aggregation. Agent sends query parameters → flow handles pagination + processing → returns summary.
matchKeywords: Data source has 500+ records that match the query
Capability mentions all records, full report, complete list, export
Query needs aggregation (count, sum, average) across many records
User expects a summary, not raw record listing

patterns.name: Real-Time Notifications
patterns.naive: Agent polls a data source on schedule to detect changes, then notifies users.
patterns.proven: Power Automate event-triggered flow detects the change → sends proactive message or adaptive card to Teams. Agent handles follow-up conversation.
matchKeywords: Capability mentions alert, notify, real-time, when X happens
Trigger is an external event (new record, status change, email received)
User expects notification without asking the agent first

factors.name: Conversational Need
factors.simpler: Data moved/transformed/displayed — dashboard or form suffices

factors.name: Interaction Pattern
factors.agent: Reactive with AI judgment, 40%+ need interpretation
factors.simpler: Procedural: event → pipeline of deterministic steps

factors.name: User Value of Natural Language
factors.agent: Ambiguous queries, contextual follow-ups, broad audience
factors.simpler: Structured UI (form, button, list) works equally well

factors.name: MCS Feasibility
factors.agent: Response <30s, data within limits, connectors exist
factors.simpler: Sub-second, bulk records, multi-system transactions, batch

componentPriority.examples: MCP servers, native knowledge, generative orchestration

rules.condition: All capabilities matched by Tier 1-2 first-party agents (100% coverage)
Solution type score 4-5: strong conversational need, AI judgment, NL value
Solution type score 3: CA for conversational + Power Automate for automation
Solution type score 1-2: deterministic pipeline, limited conversation need
Solution type score 0: outside MCS capabilities

solutionTypeFactors: conversationalNeed: users need dialogue vs data moved/displayed
interactionPattern: AI judgment needed vs deterministic flowchart
userValueOfNL: broad non-technical audience vs structured UI suffices
mcsFeasibility: fits MCS limits vs requires batch/sub-second/heavy compute

# MCS Component Quick Reference (for wizard context)

## Triggers
Conversational: OnConversationStart, OnRecognizedIntent, OnUnknownIntent, OnMessageActivity, OnSystemRedirect
Event (autonomous): SharePoint, OneDrive, Dataverse, Recurrence, Planner, Email, Custom connectors
Advanced: OnPlanComplete, OnGeneratedResponse, OnKnowledgeRequested (custom knowledge)
Agent flow composition: Agent Node in Agent Flows (GA Mar 2026) — call a Copilot Studio agent inline from a flow step, agent reasons over data + uses tools + optional human-in-the-loop escalation. See knowledge/cache/power-automate-integration.md.

## Channels
Available: Microsoft Teams + M365 Copilot, SharePoint, Power Pages, Demo Website, Custom Website (iframe), Custom canvas (Web SDK), Mobile app (Client SDK), Outlook (via M365 Copilot), WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger, Direct Line, Telephony (voice)
Default for internal: Teams + M365 Copilot. External: Custom website/WhatsApp.

## MCP Servers (prefer over connectors)
GA (Microsoft-built): Microsoft Dataverse, Dynamics 365 Business Central, Fin & Ops Apps (Dynamics 365), Office 365 Outlook -- Contact Management, Office 365 Outlook -- Email Management, Office 365 Outlook -- Meeting Management, Microsoft Learn Docs MCP, GitHub, ICM MCP, Process Mining
Preview (Microsoft-built): Dynamics 365 Sales MCP Server, Dynamics 365 ERP Analytics MCP, Dynamics 365 Service MCP, Fabric MCP, Power Apps MCP Server, Work IQ Mail, Work IQ User, Work IQ Calendar, Work IQ Teams, Work IQ SharePoint, Work IQ OneDrive, Microsoft SharePoint Lists MCP, Microsoft 365 Admin Center MCP, Work IQ Word, Work IQ Copilot
GA (third-party): Azure Databricks, Experlogix Smart Flows, S360 Breeze MCP
Preview (third-party): D365 Contact Center Admin MCP, Box MCP Server, Gieni TS Server MCP, Databricks, Bigdata-com, CData Connect AI, Celonis MCP Server, Cronofy MCP, Draup MCP Server, Enlyft MCP, Ezekia-MCP, Highspot MCP
Work IQ (Priority 1a): single server set — adds cross-M365 coverage. Use for any M365 data access.

## Key Connectors
M365 Standard: SharePoint (MCP alt), Outlook 365 (MCP alt), Microsoft Teams (MCP alt), OneDrive for Business (MCP alt), Planner, Excel Online, Dataverse, Salesforce
Data (Premium): SQL Server, HTTP, Azure Blob Storage, Azure OpenAI
Third-party (Premium): Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zoom Meetings (Independent Publisher), Jira, Confluence, Adobe PDF Services, Encodian, Zendesk
Rule: if a connector has "(MCP alt)", prefer the MCP server over the connector. Total catalog: 37 connectors indexed, 1400+ in Power Platform catalog.

## Knowledge Sources
Core: Public websites (25 URLs), Uploaded files (unlimited), SharePoint (25 URLs), Dataverse (unlimited), Enterprise data/Copilot connectors, Azure AI Search, Custom (OnKnowledgeRequested)
Unstructured: Salesforce, ServiceNow, Confluence, Zendesk (sync every 4-6h)
Real-time (preview): Salesforce, ServiceNow, Azure SQL, Snowflake, Databricks, Oracle, SAP, Google Sheets
Limits: 500 knowledge objects/agent, 25 source limit for gen orchestration (uploaded files exempt), 5 source types max

## Models
GA: GPT-4.1 [general], GPT-5 Chat [general], Claude Sonnet 4.5 [general], Claude Sonnet 4.6 [general], Claude Opus 4.6 [deep], GPT-4o mini [general], GPT-4o [general]
Preview: GPT-5 Reasoning [deep], GPT-5 Auto [auto]
Experimental (US early-access, not for prod): GPT-5.3 Chat [general], GPT-5.4 Reasoning [deep], GPT-5.5 Reasoning [deep], Claude Opus 4.7 [deep], Grok 4.1 Fast [general]
Retired: GPT-4o [general]
Default: GPT-4.1 (GA, all regions). Preview/Experimental require admin enablement (preview + external-models + cross-geo).

M365 Copilot channel limitations surfaced (no OnConversationStart, no GIF/basic cards/video/file/speech, no Action.Execute adaptive cards, inactivity trigger fires but can't post, no reactions). Adaptive Cards: v1.6 schema in default Web Chat (no Action.Execute), v1.5 in Teams and Omnichannel. MC1282727: Teams classic agent creation retirement (scheduled Apr 1 2026) paused, timeline TBD. Apr 24, 2026 doc refresh: adaptive-cards-overview re-confirmed schema versions (no new versions). Mar 2026 accessibility best practices for Adaptive Cards live (screen readers, keyboard nav, Teams-specific scenarios)."

Schema v1.6 remains latest (no v1.7). Copilot Studio VS Code extension (GA Jan 2026) — clones CS agents locally; for CA not DA. ## First-Party Agents (recommend before building)

- Analyst (Tier 1, GA (July 2025)): Analyze this data and find trends; Create charts/visualizations from spreadsheet
- Word Agent (Tier 2, GA (rolling out 2026)): Generate a [report/proposal/memo] document; Draft a [policy/procedure/guide] based on [context]
- Excel Agent (Tier 2, GA (rolling out 2026)): Create a spreadsheet tracking [items]; Build a budget/forecast template
- PowerPoint Agent (Tier 2, GA (rolling out 2026)): Create a presentation about [topic]; Build a slide deck for [meeting/audience]
- Writing Coach (Tier 3, GA): Review and improve my writing; Adjust tone of this document
- Prompt Coach (Tier 3, GA): Help me write better prompts; Optimize my Copilot queries
- Idea Coach (Tier 3, GA): Brainstorm ideas for [project]; Help me plan [initiative]

- sp-001 Web Content Extraction: Dedicated content extraction service that returns clean structured article data.
- sp-002 Document Generation: Power Automate flow with Word Online "Populate a Microsoft Word template" action
- sp-003 Iterating Over N Items: Power Automate flow with "Apply to each" action. Agent collects the list → sends
- sp-004 File Upload in Teams Channel: Stage files to SharePoint first, pass the SharePoint URL to the agent. Or use Po
- sp-005 Complex Data Transformation: Code interpreter action (if available) or Azure Function / Power Automate expres
- sp-006 Scheduled Batch Processing: Power Automate scheduled flow handles the batch. Agent is invoked only for human
- sp-007 Multi-System Orchestration: Power Automate flow with explicit action ordering, error handling per step, and 
- sp-008 API with Complex Auth: Custom connector with proper auth configuration, or Azure Function as auth proxy

## Component Priority Ladder (Microsoft-first)
Priority 1a: Work IQ (2 servers) — Work IQ Copilot + Work IQ User — covers all M365 data [cache only]
Priority 1b: Other MCS Built-In MCP — Dataverse, Dynamics 365, Fabric, GitHub, Learn Docs, Sentinel [cache only]
Priority 2: Power Platform — Power Automate flows, Dataverse, custom connectors [cache only]
Priority 3: Azure Services — Azure Functions, Azure AI, Azure Storage [cache + quick verify]
Priority 4: M365 Connectors — SharePoint, Outlook, Teams (only if Work IQ unavailable) [cache only]
Priority 5: Certified Premium — Dynamics 365, ServiceNow, Salesforce [cache + verify availability]
Priority 6: Third-Party / Custom — Custom MCP servers, HTTP endpoints, community tools [full live research required]

## Architecture Decisions
Solution type: 5-factor score (0=not-recommended, 1-2=flow, 3=hybrid, 4-5=agent)
Architecture: 6-factor score (0-2=single-agent, 3+=multi-agent)
Build path: first-party-only → declarative-agent → custom-agent
